description: Past failure patterns, each checked against the roles and workflows as they are. A role or workflow change that loses a pattern's protection fails `fm-retro eval patterns`. `set` keeps tuning patterns (used while writing a rule) apart from the fixed test patterns the score is judged on; bin/fm-retro prints both scores. Patterns come from the Anthropic code-review and verification articles and from this repository's own history.

patterns.source: article: one CLI PR went through more than fifty review rounds overnight
patterns.pattern: review and QA loops never converge: no round cap, or a fourth round instead of the author stepping back

patterns.source: article: about 59% of what the reviewer kept flagging was code from its first pass
patterns.pattern: every re-review re-reads the whole change and re-posts old findings instead of the delta

checks.jq: (.steps.review.input | map(.from) | index("delta") != null) and (.steps.review.input | map(.from) | index("feedback-all") != null) and (.steps.review.instruction | contains("only the delta"))

checks.regex: review the DELTA since the last reviewed commit

patterns.source: article: findings are verified by other agents before humans (and implementers) see them
patterns.pattern: unverified review findings go straight back to the implementer: noise costs a commit and a round each

patterns.source: article: a passing review on an out-of-date commit means nothing
patterns.pattern: a pass recorded for an older commit lets the change deliver after a later fix commit

checks.jq: (.steps.implement.commits == true) and (.steps.ship.instruction | contains("THIS commit")) and (.gates.commit != null)

checks.regex: A stale pass, a missing gate

patterns.source: article: if a change can modify the check that judges it, the check is broken
patterns.pattern: a gate reads its rules from the change under review, so the change can edit the rules that judge it

checks.jq: (.steps.classify.instruction | contains("BASE branch")) and (.steps.qa.instruction | contains("BASE branch")) and (.steps.review.instruction | contains("BASE branch"))

patterns.source: article: never let a bot approval replace a required human one
patterns.pattern: an agent verdict (QA, review, release, or the Captain) is treated as the human approval a risky change requires

checks.jq: (.steps.ship.instruction | contains("never replaces a human")) and (.steps.deliver.instruction | contains("Never merge"))

patterns.source: brief: a security review that can block when the change touches a sensitive surface
patterns.pattern: a change that touches a sensitive surface skips the security review, or the security gate cannot block

checks.regex: Any sensitive surface means tier at least medium

patterns.source: article: When we change direction - raise it early, not as a blocking comment on a finished PR
patterns.pattern: a wrong approach is discovered late and ground through: a step has no early change-direction outcome

patterns.source: article: ask the agent to show the output instead of saying it is done
patterns.pattern: the implementer reports done with no command output, and review starts on unverified work

patterns.source: article: Claude cannot skip flaky tests or weaken a check to pass it
patterns.pattern: the fixer weakens or deletes the regression test that was meant to gate the fix

checks.jq: (.roles.tester != .roles.implementer) and (.steps.fix.instruction | contains("Do not edit that test")) and (.steps.qa.instruction | contains("IMPORTANT finding"))

patterns.source: article: refactors are verified by differential tests with the old system as the oracle
patterns.pattern: a refactor changes behavior and nothing compares old and new

checks.jq: (.steps.qa.instruction | contains("behavior must be unchanged")) and (.steps.refactor.instruction | contains("BEFORE"))

patterns.source: article: running the app end to end matters more than tests; UI is checked in a real browser
patterns.pattern: a UI change is verified by reading code or unit tests, never in a browser

patterns.source: official FirstMate AGENTS.md section 7: no-mistakes alone owns review; no second manual reviewer
patterns.pattern: the forced workflow stacks a second manual reviewer or a blocking gate on top of no-mistakes

patterns.source: primary policy section 6: bounded helpers only, one level, no widened authority
patterns.pattern: a leaf role gains the task tool (recursion), or a spawning role loses its allow-list

checks.jq: ((.tools | index("task")) != null) and ((.spawns | length) > 0) and ((.spawns | index("fm-lead")) == null)

patterns.source: article: findings are voted on; only enough agreement posts them; style-only is dropped
patterns.pattern: the verifier drops a finding without evidence, or leaves a handed finding unaccounted for

checks.regex: Every drop has a reason from the list and evidence

patterns.source: article: Important, Nit, Pre-existing: a bug the PR did not introduce must not read as the author's fault
patterns.pattern: style or cleanup findings block the author, or a pre-existing bug is blamed on the author

checks.regex: A defect that predates the change is PRE-EXISTING

patterns.source: article: the improvement loop proposes through a PR and a human approves; nothing auto-applies
patterns.pattern: the improver edits a role or a gate directly, from inside a running task

patterns.source: article: start any new gate in observe mode before enforce, with a bounded blocked-twice-then-allow escape
patterns.pattern: a new gate ships enforcing, so a false positive wedges every run

patterns.source: past incident #32: the Captain chose skills per task and the lists drifted
patterns.pattern: skills are chosen per task instead of coming with the role, or a role exceeds the skill budget

patterns.source: primary policy section 6: the parent keeps verification; macro orchestration stays with FirstMate
patterns.pattern: the lead replaces the workflow's independent QA and review, or drives the workflow itself

checks.regex: independent QA, review and security steps
